text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
***GENERAL***
ALL PAPERS
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said opposition Young Democrats leader Viktor Orban's recent remarks jeopardize the basic goals of Hungarian foreign policy.
- Documents of the communist state security will be open for research and for tose who think they were under observation.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Hungary's Army and Air Force will be separated as of September 1.
MAGYAR NEMZET
- Latest poll shows opposition Young Democrats leading with 30 percent, closely followed by the ruling Socialists with 29 percent and Smallholders third with 20 percent.
***BUSINESS***
ALL PAPERS
- June industrial output was up 7.8 percent year-on-year and 5.4 percent month-on-month.
- Hungary's wheat crop is estimated to be five million tonnes this year.
- Foreign oil companies started a concerted effort to break MOL's dominance in the Hungarian market.
- Privatisation agency APV Rt will probably sell a large package of its remaining stake in Kereskedelmi es Hitelbank (K&H) before the end of the year.
- Primagaz increased its first half net profit to 827 million forints from 651 million in the same period of 1996.
- Liquor manufacturer Zwack Unicum RT struggles to hold its position in a shrinking market.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Mobile phone operator Pannon GSM almost doubled its revenue to 13.34 billion forints in the first half of 1997 compared with 7.29 billion in the same period of 1996.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The pension may break even this year.
